title: Internal and External Training Load: 15 Years On
authors: Impellizzeri FM, Marcora SM, Coutts AJ
journal: International Journal of Sports Physiology and Performance
population: Conceptual commentary on training-load constructs in athletes
findings: Exercise is a stressor inducing psychophysiological responses that mediate cellular adaptations, so coaches and scientists need to control the stress applied at the individual level.
In 2003 the authors introduced a framework in which training load has two measurable components: internal and external load.
The commentary extends, clarifies and refines the framework and the definitions of internal and external load to avoid misinterpretation.
limitations: Conceptual commentary with no new data; the abstract states no quantitative findings and the refined definitions are in the full text, which was not read.
implications: Keep the data model split into external load (distance, duration, pace, elevation, running power) and internal load (HR-based TRIMP, sRPE), and never present an external metric as physiological stress.
Compute adaptation-oriented features from internal load and mechanical/volume features from external load, stored separately.
No numeric parameter is justified by this paper.

verification.notes: Crossref confirms title, IJSPP, Feb 2019, first author Impellizzeri. Findings limited to the abstract.
